bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Shift in consumer preferences — Evolving consumer behaviour driven by digital adoption and lifestyle changes may impact demand for traditional stationery and art products.
- Raw material cost fluctuation — Variability in global supply chains and inflationary pressures, including geopolitical disruptions, may result in increased input costs, affecting margins.
- Demand seasonality — Sales performance is influenced by academic cycles and festive periods, resulting in seasonal fluctuations in demand.
- Brand relevance — Sustaining brand resonance among younger and digitally engaged consumers remains essential in a competitive environment.
- Regulatory and policy changes — Changes in education policies, trade regulations, and environmental norms may impact compliance requirements and operational processes.
- Competitive environment — Intense competition from domestic stationery brands may impact market share, pricing power, and margins.
- Inventory record-keeping / internal control weakness — The statutory auditors issued a modified (qualified) opinion after management identified discrepancies between the physical quantity recorded in the books and the physical inventory in the prior year (an expense including indirect taxes of Rs 2,356.81 lakhs was recognised); the possible impact on prior-period comparability could not be determined, affecting comparability of the current year's figures.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body: The Company operates three manufacturing facilities at Patalganga, Tarapur and Jammu, and its disclosed capex activity during the year was directed at energy-conservation and process-upgrade initiatives rather than named capacity-expansion projects. At Patalganga, a 564 KWp solar power plant was installed and commissioned (in addition to 517 KWp installed in previous years), together contributing approximately 46.5% of the plant's total power consumption in FY26; diesel generator usage was also reduced following commissioning of an express feeder power line. At Tarapur, a 500 KWp solar power plant was installed contributing approximately 50% of the facility's power requirement, with a further 200 KWp solar plant recently commissioned at the same site, and a briquette-fired hot water generator was introduced to replace electrical heating. Across factories, electric injection moulding machines are replacing hydraulic machines, treated effluent from ETPs is recycled and reused (yielding approximately 20% water savings), and a 65,000-litre rainwater storage pond has been established at Patalganga. R&D spend was Rs 636.10 lakhs in FY26 versus Rs 554.33 lakhs in FY24-25, directed largely at improving environmental and social impact given the Company's child/student end-user base.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's stationery industry is projected to reach Rs.45,000-48,000 crore by 2026, remaining one of the largest global markets by volume, driven by a large student base and an exam-oriented education system.
- The organised segment (branded players and established distributors) is gaining traction in urban and semi-urban markets, while the unorganised sector continues to dominate price-sensitive rural and local markets.
- Premiumisation trends are enabling higher value realisation despite pressure on low-cost paper products.
- E-commerce and modern retail are expanding access and enabling new consumption patterns.
- Education stationery remains the largest, highly seasonal segment linked to the academic cycle; office stationery demand is stable across corporates, MSMEs and government; art and creative supplies is a smaller but faster-growing segment with higher value potential.
- Globally, rising education enrolment, ESG-driven adoption of recycled/sustainable products, omnichannel retail, and innovation (reusable, refillable, biodegradable products) are cited as key demand drivers for the stationery category.
